Quirk Damage and Insurance.text: When a Quirk damages property, someone pays, and who pays depends on who used it and why. A civilian who breaks something with a Quirk, by accident or on purpose, owes the owner for it; Quirk liability insurance, sold with renters', home and business policies, covers accidents, and insurers ask about a customer's registered Quirk and price the premium by its risk, so a fire or explosion Quirk costs more to insure. Deliberate damage is not covered. Damage done by a licensed hero in lawful duty is covered by the agency's liability insurance and a government compensation fund, unless the force was reckless, in which case the hero and agency can face claims. Damage caused by villains is charged to the offender in court, but victims usually recover through their own insurance or public disaster relief, since few villains can pay. Claims after a big hero fight take months, and shop owners say so on the news.
